Chapter 7 • Metric

7.4 Curvature of the Metric

  • From now on, \(\mathrm{Riem}\) and \(\mathrm{Ric}\) denote the curvatures of \(\nabla^{\text{LC}}\), both determined by \(g\) through \(g \longrightarrow \nabla^{\text{LC}} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Riem} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Ric}\). Using \(g\) once more, through \(\flat\), \(\flat^{-1}\) or \(g\) itself, we define:

    1. The Riemann–Christoffel curvature, the \((0,4)\)-tensor field \[ \mathrm{Riem}^\flat(\mathcal{W}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \coloneqq \mathrm{Riem}\big( \flat(\mathcal{W}), \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y} \big), \qquad (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ajkm} = g_{al} \, \mathrm{Riem}^l_{jkm} , \] the components following from \(\flat(\partial x_a) = g_{al} \, dx^l\).

    2. The Ricci scalar, the scalar field (chart independent, as \(\mathrm{Ric}\)) \[ R \coloneqq \mathrm{Ric}\big( \flat^{-1}(dx^m), \partial x_m \big) = (g^{-1})^{mk} \, \mathrm{Ric}_{km} \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M}), \] using \(\flat^{-1}(dx^m) = (g^{-1})^{mk} \, \partial x_k\).

    3. The Einstein curvature, the \((0,2)\)-tensor field \[ G \coloneqq \mathrm{Ric} - \frac{1}{2} \, R \, g , \qquad G_{ab} = \mathrm{Ric}_{ab} - \frac{1}{2} \, R \, g_{ab} . \]
